overview: Arts/Design is the one program family across this 15-country package where a non-academic gate -- a portfolio, an audition, a talent/aptitude exam -- is plausibly the primary selection mechanism rather than a secondary factor. That is true, but unevenly, and the axis that determines 'true' is mostly not country -- it is which institutional/qualification system the specific programme sits inside. Three mechanism shapes recur: (1) REPLACES -- the portfolio/audition/aptitude exam is the primary or dominant mechanism and the academic-qualification requirement is reduced to a soft/nominal floor, or can be waived outright for a strong artistic result (sharpest: Germany's Kunsthochschulen, where a strong aptitude-exam result substitutes for the Abitur itself; also Netherlands' HBO kunstvakonderwijs, Italy's AFAM sector, France's Beaux-Arts de Paris and Conservatoire de Paris, Spain's Ensenanzas Artisticas Superiores, the UK's Conservatoires-scheme institutions, the US's dedicated conservatories, Canada's OCAD University, and Australia's NIDA/VCA). (2) ADDS A HARD GATE, DOES NOT REPLACE -- the portfolio/audition is real and separately assessed but sits alongside the country's normal score/points mechanism, which still fully applies (Ireland's NCAD-type courses, New Zealand's Auckland creative programmes, Hong Kong's HKAPA, parts of Singapore's Autonomous-University sector). (3) SAME AS GENERAL ADMISSION -- no arts-specific gate at all (Spain's Bellas Artes Grado at public universities; Architecture at ordinary Italian universities). The single most important structural finding: shape (1) vs (3) does not track country -- it tracks whether the programme sits inside the ordinary university/degree system or a parallel, separately governed arts-education sector with its own qualification track. Four countries show this identical parallel-sector shape (Germany, Italy, France, Spain -- Netherlands shows a milder version). Turkey is the deliberate exception that sharpens rather than contradicts the pattern: its conservatory exception sits inside the same unified YKS system rather than a separate sector.

countries.scope: institution-type-dependent, not a single national rule -- verify per institution (comprehensive university vs. dedicated conservatory vs. dedicated art/design college)
countries.description: The base country doc's holistic-review framing already lists portfolios/auditions as one factor among several at ordinary comprehensive universities -- accurate and unrevised here. Dedicated single-discipline institutions are a different case, not a stricter version of the same case. Juilliard: SAT/ACT not required for US or international applicants, and in most cases no specific courses, GPA, standardized test scores, or class rank required at all -- only completed secondary education (diploma or GED) and the discipline-specific audition itself. This is close to a pure audition-only mechanism, a genuine override of the US's own holistic-multi-factor framing for this institutional category. RISD sits in between: still Common-App-routed, still requiring transcript and recommendation letters, but the portfolio (12-20 work samples via SlideRoom) is the decisive discriminator layered onto -- not replacing -- the normal application file.
countries.eligibility_determinants: Completed secondary education (diploma or GED) as a floor; the discipline-specific audition (Juilliard) or portfolio (RISD) as the operative selection mechanism. Juilliard sets no minimum GPA, course pattern, or standardized test score at all.
countries.strengthens_application: A strong, disciplined audition/portfolio matched to the specific institution's stated requirements; at multi-component institutions like RISD, a coherent transcript/essay/recommendation file still supports the portfolio rather than being irrelevant.
countries.largely_irrelevant: SAT/ACT scores at dedicated conservatories (explicitly not required at Juilliard); broad extracurricular breadth beyond the discipline itself; GPA competitiveness beyond basic completion at audition-primary institutions.
countries.never_infer: Do not assume a comprehensive university's art/design/music department (portfolio as one holistic factor) works the same way as a dedicated conservatory or art college (portfolio/audition as the dominant or sole mechanism) -- both exist under the same country's general admissions architecture but are structurally different populations.

countries.scope: UAL/Conservatoires-scheme institutions specifically, distinct from mainstream UCAS-Tariff-offer courses
countries.description: UAL/Conservatoires-scheme institutions sit outside the ordinary UCAS-Tariff-offer mechanic. Central Saint Martins (UAL) BA Fine Art requires a Level-3 qualification (Foundation Diploma in Art & Design, BTEC Extended Diploma MPP, or equivalent -- A-levels/IB alone are explicitly not accepted without also holding a Foundation Diploma or equivalent) plus three GCSEs at grade 4+, and states entry 'will also be determined by assessment of your portfolio' -- both required, with a named exception pathway for strong-portfolio applicants who miss standard entry requirements. Royal College of Music (a UCAS Conservatoires-scheme institution, a separate application service from mainstream UCAS Undergraduate) sets an academic floor of just two A-levels at grade E or above -- the lowest passing UK grade -- while stating 'the main basis for admission... is your performance at audition.' Royal College of Art has historically been graduate-only with no undergraduate provision at all (changing from September 2027 via a joint programme with Norwich University of the Arts, not yet operative).
countries.eligibility_determinants: A Level-3-equivalent qualification floor (UAL) or a nominal A-level pass floor (RCM: grade E) plus the portfolio (UAL) or audition (RCM) as the deciding factor.
countries.strengthens_application: A strong, well-curated portfolio (UAL) or audition performance (RCM/conservatoires); holding a Foundation Diploma in Art & Design ahead of a UAL application; preparing repertoire to each conservatoire's own specified requirements, since UCAS Conservatoires still requires individual auditions per institution despite the shared application front-end.
countries.largely_irrelevant: Competitive UCAS Tariff points at Conservatoires-scheme institutions (RCM's academic bar is a nominal pass, not a competitive score); a plain A-level/IB record without a Foundation Diploma or equivalent for most UAL courses.
countries.never_infer: Do not assume the Royal College of Art currently offers, or has ever offered, undergraduate admission -- it has been graduate-only historically, changing only from September 2027. Do not assume UCAS Conservatoires functions like mainstream UCAS Undergraduate -- it is a separate service, and audition performance (not predicted grades) is the defining mechanic.

countries.scope: HBO kunstvakonderwijs sector (Rietveld Academie, conservatoria) as distinct from the WO VWO-equivalence baseline
countries.description: Nearly all Dutch Bachelor's-level art/design/conservatoire education sits in the HBO (kunstvakonderwijs) tier, not the WO tier the base country doc's VWO-equivalence baseline describes -- so the precise finding is not that VWO-equivalence is 'waived' for a WO institution, but that arts education is structurally an HBO-tier discipline carrying that tier's own lower floor. Rietveld Academie's own page confirms the stated minimum is 'EQF level 4 or higher (equivalent to Dutch Havo or Mbo4)' -- below VWO -- with the deciding factor for the first admission round being a wide, diverse portfolio of visual work. The real structural break is that, unlike ordinary HBO admission (Havo-equivalent threshold met = admitted, mirroring VWO/WO), arts-education admission stays competitive and portfolio/audition-driven above that floor -- breaking the Dutch 'eligible = admitted' pattern the same way numerus fixus does, via a different selection tool. Royal Conservatoire The Hague confirms the audition is the operative mechanism directly: a two-part (theoretical+practical) entrance exam, programme-specific (e.g. Bachelor Vocal Studies: a 20-minute, >=2-language audition programme, a separate poem recording, a pass/fail theory test), jury-assessed on vocal level/musicality/expressiveness, not a grades-based ranking.
countries.eligibility_determinants: An EQF level 4 / Havo-or-Mbo4-equivalent floor (lower than the VWO baseline used for WO admission generally) plus passing the institution's own portfolio review and/or audition, which is the actual competitive mechanism above that floor.
countries.strengthens_application: A diverse, recent (within ~3 years) portfolio of visual work (Rietveld); a well-prepared, stylistically varied audition programme plus strong sight-reading/theory performance (Royal Conservatoire).
countries.largely_irrelevant: VWO-level academic attainment beyond the lower HBO/kunstvakonderwijs floor -- meeting the higher WO-track VWO bar is not required and does not substitute for portfolio/audition quality.
countries.never_infer: Do not describe Dutch art/conservatoire admission as 'VWO-equivalence waived' -- the more precise fact is that this education sits in the (already lower-floor) HBO tier by design, and the structural break from the rest of the Dutch system is that eligibility does not equal admission here, unlike ordinary HBO/WO threshold programmes.

countries.scope: AFAM sector (Accademie di Belle Arti, Conservatori, dance academies) as a parallel higher-education sector distinct from the MUR-university system
countries.description: AFAM (Alta Formazione Artistica, Musicale e Coreutica) is a parallel higher-education sector, governed separately from the ordinary MUR-university system the base Italy doc's TOLC/CEnT-S/IMAT/semestre-filtro findings describe. AFAM admission requires a secondary diploma (or foreign-equivalent with an Italian embassy declaration of value) as a floor, plus a test di ammissione, which is the operative selection mechanism -- with a narrower carve-out than Germany's: holders of specific arts-track diplomas (Artistic Maturity/Liceo Artistico, Applied Arts diploma, Art Institute License, Experimental Artistic High School) are exempt from the admission interview specifically, not the whole test. Architecture -- sometimes casually grouped with 'creative' fields -- is explicitly NOT part of AFAM; it remains a TOLC-based, numero-chiuso University-sector programme like Engineering, with no portfolio step confirmed.
countries.eligibility_determinants: A secondary diploma (or recognised foreign equivalent) as a floor, plus passing the institution's own test di ammissione (portfolio/practical + interview, with narrow diploma-based interview exemptions).
countries.strengthens_application: A strong practical/portfolio result at the test di ammissione; holding one of the named arts-track diplomas that exempts the candidate from the interview component specifically.
countries.largely_irrelevant: TOLC/CEnT-S-style standardized test performance -- these are University-sector instruments, not part of the AFAM admission mechanism.
countries.never_infer: Do not assume Architecture is part of the AFAM/portfolio-gated pathway merely because it is a design-adjacent, sometimes 'creative'-labelled field -- it is governed by the ordinary numero-chiuso University mechanism (TOLC-based), not AFAM's test di ammissione.

countries.scope: Kunsthochschulen/Musikhochschulen, a separate Hochschulart from the Land's ordinary Universitat sector
countries.description: Kunsthochschulen (art academies) and Musikhochschulen (music academies) are their own Hochschulart, institutionally and legally separate from the ordinary Universitat sector the base country doc's NC/Abitur/Anabin framework describes. Muthesius Kunsthochschule's own admissions guidance states directly that applicants WITHOUT the Abitur can study there if they pass the artistic aptitude exam (Eignungspruefung) with a grade better than 2.0 -- confirmed as the sole qualifying pathway for non-Abitur applicants: a sufficiently strong Eignungspruefung result substitutes for the general university-entrance qualification entirely. Even for Abitur-holders, the Mappe (portfolio, ~15-30 work samples) plus the Eignungspruefung (portfolio review + practical tasks + colloquium) is the dominant selection mechanism -- Abitur grade is not used competitively the way it is for NC-Medicine's AdH quota. Musikhochschulen use the equivalent practical instrument: a live or video-pre-selected Vorspiel (audition).
countries.eligibility_determinants: Either the Abitur (or recognised equivalent) OR a sufficiently strong Eignungspruefung result (better than a 2.0 grade at Muthesius specifically) -- the aptitude exam can substitute for the academic qualification entirely for non-Abitur applicants. For all applicants, the Mappe/Eignungspruefung (art) or Vorspiel (music) is the operative selection mechanism.
countries.strengthens_application: A strong Mappe (15-30 work samples showing conceptual depth, technical skill, personal development) and strong performance across the Eignungspruefung's practical-task and colloquium components; for music, audition/Vorspiel quality.
countries.largely_irrelevant: Abitur grade/GPA competitiveness once the aptitude-exam pathway is in play -- for non-Abitur applicants it is irrelevant by definition, and even for Abitur-holders it is not used competitively the way NC-Medicine uses Abiturnote.
countries.never_infer: Do not assume Kunsthochschule/Musikhochschule admission requires the Abitur -- this is the single confirmed case in this research pass where a talent exam literally substitutes for the general academic qualification, not merely supplements or lowers the bar for it.

countries.scope: institution/discipline-dependent within the country -- specialist art/design colleges (OCAD U) vs. music/design departments inside comprehensive universities
countries.description: OCAD University's own admissions page states plainly that 'the primary basis for admission to OCAD University's studio-based degree programs (BDes or BFA) is a portfolio submission' -- the academic side is reduced to a floor (Ontario Secondary School Diploma, six 4U/M courses, 70% overall average, 70% minimum in 4U English) rather than a competitive-ranking input; portfolio quality differentiates candidates above that floor. This is a clean, primary-sourced replace finding, sharper than the base country doc's own hedged 'sometimes in place of a general personal statement' language. Music programmes at comprehensive universities (University of Toronto Faculty of Music, UBC Music) sit closer to the adds-a-hard-gate shape instead: audition and typically an interview, layered onto the university's general/faculty admission requirements, per the base country doc -- not independently re-verified as a full replacement this pass.
countries.eligibility_determinants: A completion-level academic floor (e.g. OCAD U: OSSD, six 4U/M courses, 70% average, 70% in 4U English) that functions as a gate, not a ranking input; the portfolio is the actual competitive/decisive mechanism above that floor at specialist institutions.
countries.strengthens_application: A portfolio demonstrating skill, curiosity, and creative thinking across a diverse range of mediums (OCAD U's own stated criteria); strong audition/interview performance for music programmes at comprehensive universities.
countries.largely_irrelevant: A competitive admission average above the stated floor at portfolio-primary institutions -- OCAD U explicitly frames the average as a threshold, not a ranking factor.
countries.never_infer: Do not assume Canada's general 'separate faculty/programme application' pattern (RULE-ADMISSIONS-010) means Fine Art/Design admission works like Engineering's own supplementary-application model -- at OCAD U specifically, the portfolio is stated as the primary basis for admission, not one input alongside a competitive average.

countries.scope: ZHdK (Fachhochschule/HES-tier arts institution) -- confirmed distinct from the ~12 core cantonal universities/ETHs the base country doc's general template describes
countries.description: ZHdK (Zurich University of the Arts) requires both a secondary-education qualification equivalent to Swiss Matura (or a recognised foreign equivalent) AND a separate, discipline-specific entrance exam/portfolio. ZHdK's own page frames these as sequential, additive requirements -- the academic qualification appears to be a prerequisite for advancing to the audition stage -- rather than the academic side being waivable for strong artistic talent, the way Muthesius Kunsthochschule confirms for Germany. No Abitur-style substitution mechanism was found for ZHdK this pass -- read as a genuine, current-evidence-based contrast with Germany, not a confirmed structural absence, since ZHdK's full Regulatory Framework document was not independently fetched this session.
countries.eligibility_determinants: A Matura-equivalent secondary qualification as a confirmed prerequisite, plus passing a discipline-specific entrance exam/portfolio/audition as the operative selection layer on top.
countries.strengthens_application: A strong discipline-specific portfolio and entrance-exam/practical-task performance, once the academic prerequisite is satisfied.
countries.largely_irrelevant: Not independently confirmed this pass -- no evidence surfaced either way on whether academic grades beyond the Matura-equivalence floor matter competitively at ZHdK.
countries.never_infer: Do not assume Switzerland's art/design sector mirrors Germany's Kunsthochschule pattern of waiving the academic qualification entirely for talented applicants -- no such mechanism was confirmed at ZHdK this pass, and the two should not be treated as equivalent without further verification.

countries.scope: Beaux-Arts de Paris and Conservatoire de Paris (CNSMDP) specifically, both confirmed as running their own selection process distinct from ordinary Parcoursup-Licence ranking
countries.description: Beaux-Arts de Paris joined Parcoursup in 2023, but Parcoursup functions here purely as the submission/routing channel, not the decision mechanism -- actual admission is the school's own 2-stage competition: an eligibility stage (digitised portfolio, ~2,000-character letter of intent, CV, optional video, submitted via Parcoursup) followed by an admission stage where an on-site jury selects candidates. Structurally the same 'Parcoursup-as-intake-channel-only' shape RULE-ADMISSIONS-002/010 already document for CPGE, just compressed into the initial application rather than deferred to a later concours. The Conservatoire de Paris (CNSMDP) is confirmed NOT routed through Parcoursup at all -- admission is via the school's own competitive concours (reported ~22% overall admission rate, one cited cycle); a Sorbonne-Universite partnership lets admitted 1st-cycle students additionally earn an actual Bachelor's title if they separately also satisfy Sorbonne's own enrolment conditions.
countries.eligibility_determinants: For Beaux-Arts de Paris: passing the 2-stage eligibility (portfolio/letter/CV) then admission (jury) competition, submitted via Parcoursup as a channel only. For CNSMDP: passing the school's own concours entirely outside Parcoursup, subject to discipline-specific age limits and a cap of three attempts per discipline.
countries.strengthens_application: A strong digitised portfolio and compelling letter of intent (Beaux-Arts de Paris); strong audition/performance at the CNSMDP concours.
countries.largely_irrelevant: Parcoursup 'attendus'-style fit criteria used for ordinary Licences -- Beaux-Arts de Paris's real selection is its own jury process, not an attendus-based ranking; CNSMDP has no Parcoursup involvement of any kind.
countries.never_infer: Do not assume Beaux-Arts de Paris's presence on Parcoursup since 2023 means it is evaluated like an ordinary Licence -- Parcoursup is the submission channel only, and the actual decision runs on the school's own portfolio-and-jury concours. Do not assume every conservatoire-style institution is reachable via Parcoursup at all -- CNSMDP confirms some are not.

countries.scope: Split within the country by qualification sector -- Bellas Artes as an ordinary university Grado (no arts-specific gate) vs. Ensenanzas Artisticas Superiores (conservatorio/danza/arte dramatico, a separate qualification system)
countries.description: Bellas Artes (Fine Arts) as an ordinary Grado at a public university is confirmed, at two independent institutions, to have NO aptitude/portfolio test at all: Universidad Complutense de Madrid's own Faculty of Fine Arts page states its earlier specific entrance exam was abolished by Faculty Board agreement in 2008/09 in favour of the Selectividad/EBAU grade criterion, and Universidad de Barcelona is independently confirmed the same way -- both use the ordinary nota de admision / Distrito Unico mechanism, identical to any other Spanish Grado. Music, dance, and dramatic art higher education instead sit in an entirely separate qualification system -- Ensenanzas Artisticas Superiores, governed under its own arts-education legal framework rather than Real Decreto 534/2024's ordinary-university Grado framework -- requiring a prueba especifica de acceso as the operative mechanism. Confirmed at the Real Conservatorio Superior de Musica de Madrid (Bachillerato-or-equivalent plus a specialty-specific access test) and at multiple Conservatorios Superiores de Danza, where candidates may qualify via the standard route OR, in autonomous communities that authorise it with Ministry approval, via a 'prueba excepcional para aspirantes sin requisitos academicos' that waives the academic-diploma requirement entirely for exceptional talent.
countries.eligibility_determinants: For Bellas Artes (Grado): the identical EBAU/PAU-based nota de admision mechanism as any other Spanish degree -- no arts-specific gate exists. For Ensenanzas Artisticas Superiores (conservatorio/danza): Bachillerato-or-equivalent (or, exceptionally in some regions, a waived academic requirement) plus passing the specialty-specific prueba especifica de acceso.
countries.strengthens_application: For Bellas Artes: an ordinary competitive EBAU/nota-de-admision result, exactly as for any other degree. For conservatorio/danza: strong specialty-specific audition/practical performance at the prueba especifica de acceso.
countries.largely_irrelevant: A portfolio or artistic aptitude test for Bellas Artes at a public university -- confirmed not to exist at UCM or UB; EBAU/nota-de-admision competitiveness for conservatorio/danza programmes, which run an entirely separate access mechanism.
countries.never_infer: Do not assume Spanish Fine Arts (Bellas Artes) admission uses a portfolio or aptitude test by analogy to the Netherlands/Germany/Italy pattern -- confirmed absent at two public universities. Do not assume conservatorio/danza admission uses the EBAU/nota-de-corte mechanism -- it is a wholly separate qualification system with its own access test, and in some regions can waive the academic-diploma requirement entirely.

countries.scope: Programme-level, within one institution (NCAD) -- restricted studio programmes REPLACE the CAO points mechanism outright; two named non-restricted programmes ADD an optional portfolio as bonus points; one named programme (Visual Culture) uses no portfolio at all
countries.description: This pass's direct check of NCAD's own official admissions pages sharpens the base country doc's hedged 'combined with, not replacing, the points mechanism' language considerably for NCAD's own restricted studio programmes specifically. NCAD's own page states: 'NCAD does not operate the Leaving Cert/CAO points scheme for programmes requiring a portfolio submission. Offers are made based on portfolio score to applicants who meet minimum academic entry requirements.' That is a genuine REPLACE mechanism -- CAO points are not used as a ranking input at all for these courses, only as a minimum-entry floor -- structurally the same shape as the Netherlands/Germany pattern. NCAD is also a concrete, sourced illustration of programme-level variation within one institution: two named non-restricted programmes (Product Design, Interaction Design) instead treat the portfolio as optional, adding up to 200 bonus points on top of ordinary CAO points (a genuine 'adds a gate,' not a replacement); Visual Culture requires no portfolio at all (same as general admission). Three mechanisms, three named programmes, one institution. The non-EU/direct route shows a further, different pattern again (UCD's non-EU Medicine table layers an interview onto its criteria with no mention of HPAT or points at all) -- RULE-ADMISSIONS-014's 'two systems, not an override' shape once more, specific to applicant route rather than Arts/Design as such.
countries.eligibility_determinants: For NCAD restricted studio programmes: meeting minimum academic entry requirements (a floor, not a competitive input) plus a portfolio-score ranking that is the actual admission mechanism. For NCAD's Product Design/Interaction Design: ordinary CAO points, optionally boosted by up to 200 bonus points for a submitted portfolio. For Visual Culture: ordinary CAO points only.
countries.strengthens_application: For restricted studio programmes: portfolio quality is essentially the entire lever once the academic floor is met. For Product Design/Interaction Design: both competitive CAO points and an optional strong portfolio (each adds independently).
countries.largely_irrelevant: Leaving Certificate points *as a ranking mechanism* for NCAD's restricted studio programmes specifically -- confirmed not operated as a ranking input there at all, only as a minimum floor, a genuine inversion of how CAO points work everywhere else in the Irish system.
countries.never_infer: Do not apply one Irish 'portfolio combined with points' rule uniformly across all Art & Design-flagged CAO courses, or even across one institution -- NCAD alone runs three different mechanisms (replace / add-bonus / none) depending on the specific named programme, the sharpest single within-institution illustration in this entire pass that programme, not institution or country, is sometimes the only safe unit of analysis.

countries.scope: NIDA and VCA (University of Melbourne) specifically confirmed -- both bypass ATAR as a ranking mechanism entirely for creative/performing-arts admission
countries.description: NIDA (National Institute of Dramatic Art): confirmed directly that ATAR is not required for NIDA courses and NIDA does not use ATAR as a selection criterion at all -- the only academic requirement is holding (not scoring competitively on) a Higher School Certificate or equivalent; admission runs entirely on a two-round video/live audition process. Victorian College of the Arts (VCA, University of Melbourne) Bachelor of Fine Arts: there is no minimum ATAR required -- applicants must meet the university's minimum completion-level academic entry requirement (VCE-or-equivalent) and English-language requirement, and only then are ranked purely by folio and interview/audition; ATAR plays no role in ranking once the floor is cleared. Both are clean, official, primary-sourced confirmations of full replacement -- arguably the sharpest contrast with a country's own general mechanism found anywhere in this package, because Australia's general system (ATAR/selection-rank) is otherwise one of the most purely numeric, non-holistic ranking mechanisms documented in the whole package.
countries.eligibility_determinants: Holding (not scoring competitively on) a Higher School Certificate or equivalent (NIDA) or VCE-or-equivalent completion plus English-language requirement (VCA) as a floor; audition (NIDA) or folio-plus-interview (VCA) as the entire competitive/ranking mechanism above that floor.
countries.strengthens_application: A strong video/live audition across NIDA's two rounds; a strong folio matched to the chosen VCA specialisation plus strong interview performance.
countries.largely_irrelevant: ATAR score entirely -- both institutions confirm it plays no role in ranking once the completion-level floor is met, a genuine inversion of how ATAR normally functions across the rest of the Australian system.
countries.never_infer: Do not assume Australia's otherwise ATAR-dominant, minimal-holistic-review general system (no essays, minimal recommendations, extracurriculars largely absent per the base country doc) extends to creative/performing-arts admission at NIDA or VCA -- both explicitly and confirmedly bypass ATAR as a ranking tool.

countries.scope: University of Auckland creative programmes (Elam BFA, Music, Design, Dance Studies) -- confirmed as an added requirement, exact weighting versus Rank Score not confirmed
countries.description: University of Auckland creative programmes require meeting University Entrance plus the programme's own Rank Score threshold (these programmes cluster at the lower end of Auckland's published Rank Score table, 150-180) -- a real academic floor that, unlike NIDA/VCA, is not bypassed. On top of that floor, some programmes have additional requirements such as an interview, portfolio, or references, per Auckland's own admissions guidance, though the exact weighting of that additional layer relative to Rank Score was not confirmed by either the base country doc or this session's follow-up search. Read as very likely an added hard gate, not a replacement -- a genuine, stated gap, not a confirmed shape.
countries.eligibility_determinants: University Entrance plus a programme-specific Rank Score threshold (150-180 for Auckland's creative programmes) as a confirmed floor, plus an unconfirmed-weight additional interview/portfolio/references layer for some programmes.
countries.strengthens_application: Meeting or exceeding the programme's Rank Score threshold; presumably a strong portfolio/interview where required, though the actual decisiveness of this layer is unconfirmed.
countries.largely_irrelevant: Not independently confirmed this pass -- insufficient evidence to state what does not matter for these specific programmes beyond the general New Zealand pattern.
countries.never_infer: Do not assume New Zealand's creative programmes fully bypass the Rank Score mechanism the way Australia's NIDA/VCA bypass ATAR -- the Rank Score floor is confirmed to still apply; only the relative weight of any additional portfolio/interview layer is unconfirmed, not its existence as a genuine academic gate.

countries.scope: HKAPA specifically -- a specialised, non-comprehensive institution outside the 8 UGC-funded comprehensive universities the base country doc's JUPAS/non-JUPAS split describes
countries.description: HKAPA (Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts) uses its own 'Recognition of Prior Learning' (RPL) admission process: applicants must separately satisfy General Admission Requirements (HKDSE Level 3 in English and Chinese, Level 2 in Mathematics, per HKAPA's own published requirements) AND undergo verification through audition and/or interview and/or portfolio presentation and/or entry test, discipline-dependent (Dance, Drama, Music, Chinese Opera, Theatre & Entertainment Arts, Film & TV each set their own specifics). Two genuine gaps remain: whether HKAPA's local-student intake is channelled through JUPAS or sits entirely outside it, and the relative weight of the academic floor versus the audition/portfolio outcome -- neither confirmed this pass. The base doc's own gap ('no confirmed portfolio requirement for Art/Design/Architecture-type programmes') is now resolved for performing arts at HKAPA specifically, but remains open for visual-arts/design at HKU/CUHK/HKUST themselves.
countries.eligibility_determinants: General Admission Requirements (HKDSE Level 3 English/Chinese, Level 2 Mathematics) as a floor, plus discipline-specific verification via audition/interview/portfolio/entry test.
countries.strengthens_application: Strong discipline-specific audition/interview/portfolio performance; meeting or exceeding the General Admission Requirements floor.
countries.largely_irrelevant: Not independently confirmed this pass -- the relative weight of academic result versus audition/portfolio outcome is an open question, not a confirmed irrelevance.
countries.never_infer: Do not assume HKAPA's relationship to JUPAS mirrors the comprehensive universities' JUPAS/non-JUPAS split documented in the base Hong Kong doc -- unconfirmed either way this pass. Do not assume the absence of a confirmed portfolio requirement at HKU/CUHK/HKUST visual-arts/design programmes means none exists -- flagged as a genuine gap, not a confirmed absence.

countries.scope: NAFA and LASALLE (specialist arts institutions) as distinct from the six Autonomous Universities' more selective, programme-dependent use of interview/portfolio
countries.description: NAFA (Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts) and LASALLE College of the Arts are Singapore's dedicated arts institutions, structurally distinct from the six Autonomous Universities (NUS/NTU/SMU/SUTD/SIT/SUSS). Both require completed O-Level/A-Level (or equivalent) as a floor rather than a competitive-cutoff input, plus a portfolio as the clear discriminator: LASALLE's BA (Hons) process requires 10-15 original portfolio pieces, an admissions workshop, and an interview discussing the portfolio's content/inspirations/influences; NAFA similarly requires an updated art portfolio plus audition/interview for music/dance/theatre programmes. Within the Autonomous University sector, the pattern is closer to adds-a-hard-gate-selectively: SUTD is the most clearly confirmed portfolio-inclusive, holistic AU; NUS/NTU/SMU integrate interview/portfolio only for specific restricted-programme or qualification-type categories rather than broadly for Architecture/Industrial-Design-type programmes, where a portfolio requirement is plausible but not independently primary-verified.
countries.eligibility_determinants: Completed O-Level/A-Level or equivalent as a floor (NAFA/LASALLE), plus a required portfolio (10-15 pieces at LASALLE) and interview as the operative selection mechanism; within the AU sector, ordinary ranked/holistic admission with portfolio/interview added only for specific programmes (SUTD broadly; NUS/NTU/SMU selectively).
countries.strengthens_application: A strong, original portfolio (10-15 pieces at LASALLE) and the ability to discuss it articulately at interview; for SUTD, strong performance in its holistic, portfolio-inclusive process.
countries.largely_irrelevant: Competitive A-Level score ranking of the kind that drives NUS/NTU/SMU general admission -- NAFA/LASALLE treat the academic qualification as a completion floor, not a ranking input.
countries.never_infer: Do not assume Singapore's Autonomous Universities (NUS/NTU/SMU) broadly require a portfolio for Architecture/Industrial-Design-type programmes -- plausible by structural analogy but not independently verified; do not conflate NAFA/LASALLE's portfolio-primary mechanism with the AU sector's more selective, programme-dependent use of interview/portfolio.

countries.scope: state conservatory, fine-arts-faculty, sports-sciences, and some education-faculty performance-linked programmes -- the sole named non-exam-score exception inside an otherwise fully algorithmic domestic YKS placement system (see turkey.md in full)
countries.description: State conservatory, fine-arts-faculty (graphic design, painting, sculpture, traditional Turkish arts, music teaching), sports-sciences, and some education-faculty performance-linked programmes require a TYT raw-score threshold plus a talent/audition exam (ozel yetenek sinavi), set independently by each institution -- genuinely different in kind from every other Turkish domestic-pathway programme, which is placed by pure score-rank with zero interview/portfolio step, including Medicine, Law, and top Engineering. This pass could not resolve the exact, single national shape of the TYT threshold: some sources describe a split by programme (Composition/Theatre/Opera/Musicology at 180 vs. other conservatory programmes at 150), while at least one institution's own figures (Istanbul University Conservatory: 150 for Fine-Arts-High-School graduates vs. 180 for other applicants) instead suggest a split by applicant background -- both may be true simultaneously, but this was not resolved. At least one state conservatory (Giresun University) reportedly applies no minimum TYT threshold at all for specific departments, only requiring that TYT be sat. Secondary sources describe at least some private/foundation (vakif) conservatories as using purely talent-based selection with no TYT floor at all -- a more extreme replace-shape than the state hybrid, if accurate -- but this was not independently confirmed against any named vakif institution's own official guide this session.
countries.eligibility_determinants: A TYT raw-score threshold (commonly cited 150-200, but confirmed non-uniform -- varies by institution, and possibly by programme-type or applicant-background split, with at least one institution applying no threshold at all for specific departments) plus passing the institution's own talent/audition exam (ozel yetenek sinavi).
countries.strengthens_application: Strong preparation for the specific institution's audition/talent exam; for state conservatory programmes, also clearing that institution's specific TYT threshold, which must be confirmed per institution and per cycle rather than assumed from one commonly-cited figure.
countries.largely_irrelevant: AYT/OBP performance beyond the TYT-threshold gate -- unlike every other Turkish domestic programme, AYT and the diploma-derived OBP score do not drive placement here the way they do for score-ranked programmes; the talent exam is the operative differentiator once the TYT floor is cleared.
countries.never_infer: Do not treat a private/foundation (vakif) conservatory's admission mechanism as identical to a state conservatory's TYT-threshold-plus-talent-exam hybrid -- medium-confidence evidence suggests at least some vakif conservatories waive the TYT floor entirely, a materially different, more extreme mechanism that must be confirmed per institution. Do not assume a single national TYT figure (e.g. 150 or 180) applies uniformly -- confirmed to vary by institution, and at least one institution applies none at all for specific departments.

cross_cutting_patterns: The load-bearing variation axis for Arts/Design is not country-first (the axis every other program family in this package uses per RULE-ADMISSIONS-002/010) -- it is, in order: (1) which qualification sector the specific programme belongs to (ordinary university degree vs. a parallel arts-conservatoire education system with its own legal/governance framework), (2) institution, (3) discipline/programme within that institution, and only then, distantly, (4) country. Four independent countries confirm the identical parallel-sector shape: Germany (Universitat vs. Kunsthochschule/Musikhochschule), Italy (MUR-university vs. AFAM), France (Parcoursup-Licence vs. Beaux-Arts/Conservatoire-national), and Spain (university Grado vs. Ensenanzas Artisticas Superiores) -- with the Netherlands showing a milder version (WO vs. HBO kunstvakonderwijs). This is candidate new ruleset material: a `qualification_sector` field at the programme level, distinct from and more consequential than the university/programme override layers RULE-ADMISSIONS-002/010 already establish for every other family.

A parallel, non-legal version of the same pattern recurs in countries without a distinct national arts-education sector: free-standing, single-discipline institutions (Juilliard, RISD, OCAD University, NIDA, VCA, NAFA, LASALLE) behave structurally differently from art/design/music departments embedded inside comprehensive universities, even within the same country and even when both use the identical general national application architecture (Common App, UCAS, OUAC).

Turkey is the deliberate outlier that sharpens rather than contradicts the parallel-sector pattern: it is the one country in this pass where a genuine portfolio/audition gate exists WITHOUT a separate governing qualification sector -- the conservatory/fine-arts exception sits inside the same YKS/OSYM system as every other Turkish domestic programme, via a named exception to the shared placement algorithm rather than a separate agency. This confirms the parallel-sector finding is a genuine structural pattern, not an artifact of how specific European countries happen to organise their higher-education bureaucracies.

The variation axis can resolve at a grain finer than institution: Ireland's NCAD runs three different mechanisms across three named programmes at the SAME institution under the SAME national application platform (CAO) -- restricted studio programmes replace the CAO points mechanism outright (NCAD's own page: 'does not operate the Leaving Cert/CAO points scheme' for these courses), two named non-restricted programmes (Product Design, Interaction Design) treat an optional portfolio as up-to-200 bonus points added to CAO points, and Visual Culture uses no portfolio at all. This is the sharpest confirmed illustration in this pass that 'programme; not even institution' is sometimes the only safe unit of analysis for this family.

Arts/Design is not a mechanism-uniform family even within a single country -- Spain is the sharpest confirmed proof (Bellas Artes-as-Grado has zero non-academic gate; Ensenanzas Artisticas Superiores has the strongest gate found in this entire program-family research pass, including a possible academic-diploma waiver in some regions), and Italy's Architecture-vs-AFAM split confirms the same danger from the opposite direction (a field sometimes casually called 'creative' that is in fact governed by the ordinary numero-chiuso mechanism, not AFAM's).

Where the portfolio/audition mechanism genuinely REPLACES the academic-score mechanism (as opposed to merely adding a hard gate on top of it), it also inverts the normal competitiveness logic of that country's general system: a candidate who clears the (often reduced or nominal) academic floor and presents a stronger portfolio than a higher-GPA/higher-ATAR/higher-Abitur-grade competitor is not disadvantaged by the lower academic figure. This is the sharpest possible contrast in a country like Australia, whose general system (ATAR) is otherwise one of the most purely numeric, non-holistic ranking mechanisms in the entire 15-country package, yet whose flagship drama/fine-arts institutions (NIDA, VCA) confirm ATAR plays no ranking role at all once a completion floor is met.
unresolved_questions: The precise, single national shape (if one even exists) of Turkey's state-conservatory TYT threshold -- programme-type split (180 vs. 150) vs. applicant-background split (Fine-Arts-HS-graduate vs. other) -- was not resolved this pass; both framings recur in sourced secondary material without a clear primary-source tiebreaker, consistent with turkey.md's own flagged uncertainty on this exact point.

Whether Turkish vakif (foundation/private) conservatories genuinely and commonly waive the TYT floor entirely in favour of pure talent-based selection -- reported by secondary sources, not confirmed against any single named vakif institution's own official guide this session.

Whether ZHdK (or Switzerland's arts/design sector generally) has any mechanism comparable to Germany's Kunsthochschule Abitur-substitution for exceptionally talented applicants without a Matura-equivalent qualification -- ZHdK's own Regulatory Framework document, which likely contains the definitive answer, was not independently fetched this session.

Whether HKAPA's local-student intake is channelled through JUPAS or sits entirely outside it, and the relative weight HKAPA places on its HKDSE-based academic floor versus audition/portfolio/interview outcome -- neither was confirmed this pass.

Whether a confirmed portfolio requirement exists for visual-arts/design programmes (as opposed to the performing-arts programmes confirmed at HKAPA) at Hong Kong's comprehensive universities (HKU/CUHK/HKUST) -- the base country doc's own gap on this point was not closed this pass.

The exact relative weighting Auckland (or other New Zealand universities) place on portfolio/interview versus Rank Score for creative programmes -- confirmed to exist as an additional requirement, not confirmed as to how much it actually matters relative to the academic floor.

Whether NUS/NTU's Architecture, Industrial Design, and Landscape Architecture programmes (named in the base Singapore doc as ranking-position-restricted) carry a confirmed portfolio requirement specifically -- described as plausible by structural analogy in the base doc and not independently primary-verified in this pass either.
